note: Where a region's dated regime bands came from. `seeded:defranceschi-sovereignty` means the bands were taken from the Defranceschi family archive's own sovereignty.json, so for those regions the Atlas is partly the archive's research coming back and must not be cited as an independent confirmation of it; the Atlas added `filedUnder` and the notes. `unknown` means the region was written in the same first batch as the Defranceschi ground and nobody has checked. `not-recorded` (the default, for every region not listed) means this file does not say, which is not the same as independent. Source of the list: the family-sites coordination session's audit of 18 Oct 2026 and the region file's own note.

1580.why: a founding date used as the start of Spanish rule

1540.why: Osijek was Ottoman by 1540 and Virovitica fell in 1552

1500.why: a lower bound: the source gives no start for Ottoman rule here

1839.why: Wikipedia's infobox dates the republic 1839; the Boers took control of Port Natal in May 1838

1200.why: Lower bound, not a change of sovereignty: the Kingdom of Sicily dates from 1130; the mainland part was officially still the Kingdom of Sicily until 1282/1302 (Vespers, Caltabellotta), informally 'Naples' after. The era is a coarse umbrella spanning Hohenstaufen, Angevin vs Aragonese rival claims (1282-1302 war, 1435-1504), Spanish viceroys to 1714, Austrians 1714-1735, Bourbons, and the 1799 Parthenopean Republic (about 5 months). FIX: polity for 1200-1282 should be 'Kingdom of Sicily' (the mainland), 'Kingdom of Naples' only informally from 1282.

1806.why: All sources give 1806 for the change: Joseph Bonaparte entered Naples 15 Feb 1806 (crowned by Napoleon's act of 30 Mar); British troops held Calabria and won at Maida 4 Jul 1806; Massena had not pacified it until end of summer 1806; brigandage persisted under Murat. Ferdinand kept Sicily and never renounced the crown (rival claimant, British-backed). Contested for Calabria specifically.

1815.why: Ferdinand restored by the Treaty of Casalanza 20 May 1815 (Tolentino 2 or 3 May; Congress of Vienna 9 Jun 1815), but the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies is created only on 8 Dec 1816 (Wikipedia Two Sicilies and Naples infoboxes; Treccani: 1816). De facto restoration 1815 versus de jure union 1816 is a gap of about 19 months. FIX: polity for 1815-1816 should read Kingdom of Naples (restored Bourbon); 'Two Sicilies' from 8 Dec 1816. No source fetched shows a split of authority in Calabria itself in 1815-1860 apart from the 1860-61 change (covered under 1861).

1861.why: Garibaldi landed in Calabria 19 Aug 1860 and took Reggio 21 Aug (Expedition of the Thousand); plebiscite 21 Oct 1860 and annexation decree 17 Dec 1860 (Dickinson House Divided, citing Wambaugh); Gaeta capitulated 13 Feb 1861 and Civitella del Tronto 20 Mar 1861; Kingdom of Italy proclaimed 17 Mar 1861. The change of sovereignty ran Aug 1860 to Mar 1861. Allied landings at Reggio 3 Sep 1943 (Operation Baytown) were under the Italian armistice; sovereignty stayed with the Kingdom of Italy, so not treated as contested. FIX: 'Provincia di Vibo Valentia' is anachronistic for 1861-1995: law of 6 Mar 1992, effective 1 Jan 1996; before that Briatico was in Catanzaro province.

1200.why: Lower bound, not a sovereignty change: mainland part of the Kingdom of Sicily until 1282/1302, 'Naples' only afterwards; Angevin/Aragonese contest, French invasions 1494-1504, Spanish 1504-1714, Austrian 1714-1735, Bourbon 1735, Parthenopean Republic Jan 1799 (about 5 months). Umbrella era. FIX: polity for 1200-1282 should be 'Kingdom of Sicily'.

1806.why: Joseph Bonaparte entered Naples 15 Feb 1806, Napoleon's act naming him king 30 Mar 1806; one clean year. Contested because Ferdinand retained Sicily and the crown, with British support, until 1815.

1815.why: Ferdinand restored by the Treaty of Casalanza 20 May 1815 (Tolentino 2 or 3 May; Congress of Vienna 9 Jun 1815), but the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies is created only on 8 Dec 1816 (Wikipedia Two Sicilies and Naples infoboxes; Treccani: 1816). De facto restoration 1815 versus de jure union 1816 is a gap of about 19 months. FIX: polity for 1815-1816 should read Kingdom of Naples (restored Bourbon); 'Two Sicilies' from 8 Dec 1816. The final months 1860-61 (Naples taken 7 Sep 1860, Gaeta held by Francis II until 13 Feb 1861) are covered by the approx flag on 1861.

1861.why: Garibaldi landed in Calabria 19 Aug 1860 and took Reggio 21 Aug (Expedition of the Thousand); plebiscite 21 Oct 1860 and annexation decree 17 Dec 1860 (Dickinson House Divided, citing Wambaugh); Gaeta capitulated 13 Feb 1861 and Civitella del Tronto 20 Mar 1861; Kingdom of Italy proclaimed 17 Mar 1861. The change of sovereignty ran Aug 1860 to Mar 1861. Kingdom of Italy sovereignty continued through WWII (Allied military government administered, Badoglio government at Brindisi), so not treated as contested.

1946.why: 1946: referendum 2 Jun, provisional result 10 Jun, Umberto II left 13 Jun, Court of Cassation final result 18 Jun; Constitution in force 1 Jan 1948. One clean year for the change to a republic; monarchist appeals were rejected 12 to 7, no rival authority. FIX: the label 'Provincia di Caserta' fits Caserta/Arienzo (province re-established 1945, current form 1970) but Naples is not in it and Arpaia is not in Caserta's municipality list on Wikipedia (it is in Benevento province; not independently verified).

1200.why: Lower bound: the Kingdom of Sicily was sanctioned 1130 (County 1071). Island status shifted: Vespers war with Angevins to 1302, Aragon from 1282/1412, Savoy 1713-1720, Austria 1720-1735, Bourbons to 1816; British occupation/protection 1806-1814 (1812 constitution). Umbrella era with contested stretches; polity label 'Kingdom of Sicily' is right throughout.

1816.why: Kingdom of Sicily merged into the Two Sicilies in 1816 (Wikipedia: 8 Dec 1816 on the Naples/Two Sicilies infobox; Treccani 1816). On the island the Bourbons held the throne throughout, so one clean year. Contested: Sicily had its own independent government 12 Jan 1848 to 15 May 1849 (Bourbons retook it 15 May 1849), Messina never under the rebels; then Garibaldi from May 1860.

1861.why: Garibaldi landed at Marsala 11 May 1860, proclaimed himself Dictator of Sicily 7 Jul 1860 in Victor Emmanuel's name, conquest complete 1 Aug 1860 (Syracuse, Augusta, Milazzo); plebiscite 21 Oct 1860, annexation 17 Dec 1860, Kingdom of Italy 17 Mar 1861. Allied military government (AMGOT) ran Sicily from 10 Jul 1943 and handed administration to the Badoglio cabinet in Feb 1944, but Italian sovereignty was not transferred, so not treated as contested.

1946.why: 1946: referendum 2 Jun, provisional result 10 Jun, Umberto II left 13 Jun, Court of Cassation final result 18 Jun; Constitution in force 1 Jan 1948. One clean year for the change to a republic; monarchist appeals were rejected 12 to 7, no rival authority.

1788.why: 1788 is the founding of New South Wales (arrival 18 Jan, colony proclaimed 7 Feb 1788), not of European authority at Moreton Bay: convict settlement there began 1824 (Brisbane site 2 Dec 1824), free settlement allowed 1842. Much of the region's ground (north, west to 138E) was not administered for decades. No rival state claimant found in sources read; Indigenous sovereignty is not discussed in them.

1859.why: Queensland separation: Letters Patent signed 6 Jun 1859, but the colony was proclaimed in Brisbane 10 Dec 1859, 'separation became a legal reality' only then. Two dates six months apart; Queensland Day marks 6 June but the Queensland State Archives says the colony was born at the proclamation. Until then NSW law applied. The 1862 western boundary move (141E to 138E) is noted, and the 28 deg S border is stated differently in one Archives post (29 deg).

1901.why: Commonwealth proclaimed and Queensland became a State on 1 Jan 1901 (Constitution in force); one clean date.

1652.why: Dutch settlement at the Cape founded April 1652 (van Riebeeck); that is a founding date, not control of the district. Khoikhoi-Dutch wars 1659-60 (treaty 6 Apr 1660) and 1673-77 (peace June 1677) over land around the Fort; control of surrounding country was disputed and the Cochoqua plundered the Saldanha post in 1673. Swellendam magistracy only 1743/1745, so outer parts of the ring came under VOC rule later.

1795.why: Battle of Muizenberg 7 Aug 1795; Governor Sluysken surrendered 15 Sep 1795 (some sources say 16th); the Swellendam burghers declared a republic 17 Jun 1795 which ended 4 Nov 1795 when the British occupied the district. Rival republic on this ground, so contested.

1803.why: Sources differ on the year: Wikipedia Cape Colony and Swellendam give British rule 1795 to 1802 (Treaty of Amiens), while the Dutch Cape Colony article gives handover 1 Mar 1803 and Graaff-Reinet article says Feb 1803. No rival authority in the west found.

1806.why: Blaauwberg 8 Jan 1806, capitulation of Cape Town 10 Jan, Batavian army 18 Jan 1806; but Britain's possession was formalised only by the cession of 13 Aug 1814 (Anglo-Dutch convention; Wikipedia Cape Colony says 1814 treaty). De facto 1806, de jure 1814: gap over a year.

1910.why: Union of South Africa came into existence 31 May 1910; Cape Colony ended then.

1961.why: Republic of South Africa 31 May 1961 (1961 constitution; left Commonwealth).

1652.why: Dutch settlement at the Cape founded April 1652 (van Riebeeck); that is a founding date, not control of the district. For the eastern ground this is far earlier than any control: the Great Fish River was agreed as the boundary only in 1780 (Wikipedia: many Xhosa already lived west of it), and the Graaff-Reinet magistracy dates from 1786. FIX: for the eastern Cape the Dutch era effectively begins about 1780-1786, not 1652; the earlier ground was held by Khoikhoi and Xhosa polities.

1795.why: British took the Cape 15 Sep 1795 (Muizenberg 7 Aug). In the east the Graaff-Reinet burghers proclaimed an independent 'Colony of Graaff-Reinet' in 1795 and had to surrender to the British (no exact date in source); second Prinsloo rebellion Jan-Apr 1799, another revolt 1801. Xhosa held the Zuurveld, with the 1799-1803 war. Several authorities at once.

1803.why: Sources differ: Cape Colony article says British rule 1795-1802 (Amiens); Graaff-Reinet says Feb 1803; Dutch Cape Colony says handover 1 Mar 1803. Eastern frontier: the 1803 peace left the Xhosa in the Zuurveld, Khoi revolts and farm abandonment 1799-1803.

1806.why: Blaauwberg 8 Jan 1806, capitulation 10 Jan; formal cession 13 Aug 1814. Contested on this ground because the Zuurveld (between Great Fish and Sundays rivers) stayed with the Xhosa: reoccupied in 1811 and driven back beyond the Fish by Graham's expedition in the 1811-12 war.

1910.why: Union of South Africa came into existence 31 May 1910; Cape Colony ended then. Later wars east of the Fish are outside this ring.

1961.why: Republic of South Africa 31 May 1961. Ciskei (nominal independence 4 Dec 1981 to 27 Apr 1994, unrecognised) lay east of this ring's towns; Graaff-Reinet, Cradock and Somerset East are not in it, though the ring's eastern edge near 26.5-27E is marginal.

1538.why: Cromwell's injunction to keep registers is dated 5 Sept 1538 (Wikipedia), but a search found other sources giving 29 Sept 1538 for publication, compliance was uneven, and it was repeated in 1547 and reaffirmed in 1597; this is a record-keeping start, not a change of sovereignty. England under Henry VIII governed through Cromwell as Vicar General, no rival authority reported.

1837.why: Civil registration began 1 July 1837 (Wikipedia GRO; several family-history sites agree; one source cites 1 March 1837 as the Act's commencement, registration itself started 1 July). Registration became compulsory only in 1874/75 (Wikipedia says 1875, other sources the 1874 Act), which the era note already says. No rival authority.

1580.why: 1580 is not an event: Santa Fe city was founded 15 Nov 1573 by Garay (Wikipedia, es.wikipedia). The 'Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata' did not exist until 1 Aug 1776; before that the land belonged to the Viceroyalty of Peru. No source found for conditions on the Rosario ground in 1580, so contested is left unassessed.

1810.why: Buenos Aires Junta ended viceregal rule in Buenos Aires on 25 May 1810 but Montevideo kept a rival viceroy until 1814 and Spain only recognised Argentina in 1860 (Wikipedia). Santa Fe stayed under Buenos Aires after 1810, began autonomy in 1815 and declared sovereignty on 10 May 1816, treaty with Buenos Aires 28 May 1816 (es.wikipedia). A single Argentine state did not yet exist.

1889.why: No source found for the 1889 start of Santa Fe civil registration. A search snippet of a Universidad Nacional del Litoral study of Rafaela parish archives says the Province's Registro Civil officially opened in 1899 (page itself unreachable: connection refused); another snippet says Santa Fe pioneered civil marriage in 1867 (Oroño). FamilySearch wiki pages were blocked by a bot check and were not worked around. santafe.gov.ar Registro Civil page gives no start year.

1226.why: Teutonic state of Prussia is dated 1226 (Golden Bull of Rimini) on Wikipedia, but its infobox says 1230 (Prussian crusade begins) and 1234 (Bull of Rieti) also appears. 1226 is a grant of a claim, not control; the Order had to conquer the Old Prussians from 1230, so who held the ground in the early decades was contested (inferred from the 1230 crusade date).

1525.why: Treaty of Krakow 8 April 1525 ended the war; Prussian Homage 10 April 1525 made Albert Duke of Prussia, Polish fief (Wikipedia, Duchy of Prussia and Prussian Homage; both give 1525). Whether the Order or the Emperor contested it is not stated in the fetched pages, so contested is unassessed. Note the polity was a Polish fief until the Treaty of Wehlau 1657 and a kingdom from 1701, both inside this era.

1871.why: German Empire 1871 is a clean date for the sovereignty (Wikipedia, Province of East Prussia). But the province itself was merged with West Prussia into the Province of Prussia 1829-1878 and re-separated in 1878, so a 'Province of East Prussia' label is wrong for 1871-77. Interwar: Memel under League/French admin 1920, Lithuanian 1923-1939, back to Germany 1939; Dzialdowo to Poland 1920.

1945.why: Southern East Prussia under Polish administration from May 1945; province disestablished 1 Aug 1945 at Potsdam; northern part to the USSR, Konigsberg renamed Kaliningrad 1946, Memel region into the Lithuanian SSR 1945 (Wikipedia). Potsdam put it under Soviet/Polish control 'pending the final peace settlement'; final settlement only 12 Sept 1990, West Germany long held the 1937 frontiers (Oder-Neisse page).

1200.why: 1200 is a lower bound, not an event; no page fetched dates Poland's holding of Greater Poland in 1200 (the region sat inside the fragmented Piast duchies then). Contested unassessed.

1793.why: Prussia-Russia treaty 23 Jan 1793; Prussian share accepted by the Grodno Sejm 23 or 25 Sept 1793 depending on source; South Prussia dated 25 Sept 1793 (Wikipedia, Second Partition and South Prussia). Prussian troops met little resistance. BUT Szubin (Prussian from 1773) and Bydgoszcz (Netze District, Prussian from 1772) were already Prussian before 1793.

1807.why: Duchy of Warsaw created by the Treaties of Tilsit 7 and 9 July 1807 (Wikipedia). But the Greater Poland uprising of 1806 put Poles in control earlier, and Wikipedia's Greater Poland navbox ends South Prussia at 1806 while its article says 1807. Cession itself is by treaty.

1815.why: Grand Duchy of Posen established at the Congress of Vienna, 9 June 1815 (Wikipedia). The Duchy of Warsaw ended de facto in Jan 1813 (Russian occupation), de jure 9 June 1815; the Bydgoszcz article says re-annexed by Prussia in 1813, the Szubin article says 1815. Autonomy was abolished 5 Dec 1848 and renamed Province of Posen 9 Feb 1849 (or 26 April 1848 per another page), inside this era.

1871.why: Posen was already Prussian; it joined the North German Confederation in 1866 and the German Empire in 1871 (Wikipedia, Province of Posen). The sovereign (Prussia) did not change; the Empire dates cleanly to 1871. Standesamt civil registration 1 Oct 1874 not checked here.

1918.why: Greater Poland Uprising began 27 Dec 1918, most of the province taken by mid-January 1919; Trier armistice 16 Feb 1919 fixed a front; Treaty of Versailles signed 28 June 1919, in force 10 Jan 1920; Polish forces took the remaining German-held areas from 17 Jan 1920; front dissolved 8 March 1920. Szubin retaken 3 Jan 1919 (Szubin article). Bydgoszcz only passed to Poland after Versailles (1920). About 2,200 km2 stayed German as Posen-West Prussia (1922).

1939.why: Military district Sept 1939; annexation decrees 8 and 12 Oct 1939, Reichsgau Posen from 26 Oct 1939, renamed Wartheland 29 Jan 1940 (Wikipedia). The Polish government evacuated and formed a government in exile (Occupation of Poland page); the page does not state non-recognition, so contested rests on that alone. Bydgoszcz was annexed to Reichsgau Danzig-West Prussia, not Wartheland.

1945.why: Szubin taken by the Red Army 21 Jan 1945, Bydgoszcz in Jan/spring 1945 (Szubin and Bydgoszcz articles); disestablishment of the Wartheland 1 Aug 1945 at Potsdam (Wikipedia); the Province of Posen article says all historic parts were under Polish control by 1947. The Oder-Neisse dispute (West Germany claimed the 1937 frontiers) concerned lands that Poland did not hold in 1937; Posen was Polish 1920-1939, so no rival claim to this ground was found.

1181.why: Duchy of Pomerania is dated 1121 (vassal of Poland) in Wikipedia's infobox; in 1181 the dukes took the duchy as a fief of Barbarossa, a change of feudal status, not a founding. Overlordship passed Poland, then HRE 1181-85, Denmark 1185-1227, then HRE again. Danzig/Pomerelia was a separate Samboride duchy, not part of the duchy of Pomerania.

1637.why: Bogislaw XIV died 10 March 1637 and the duchy was divided between Brandenburg-Prussia and Sweden (Wikipedia), but Sweden controlled it from the 1630 Treaty of Stettin and the division was only fixed by the Peace of Westphalia 1648/1653; Sweden lost land east of the Oder in 1679 and Stettin and land south of the Peene in 1720 (Treaty of Stockholm); Denmark occupied 1715-1721.

1815.why: Province of Pomerania constituted 30 April 1815; Swedish Pomerania handed to Prussia 23 Oct 1815 after a 7 June 1815 treaty (Wikipedia), with Sweden ceding it to Denmark in 1814 (Treaty of Kiel) and exchanging it for Saxe-Lauenburg at Vienna. Stralsund region only organised 1818. Danzig was in the Province of West Prussia, not Pomerania.

1871.why: Province of Pomerania became part of the German Empire in 1871 (Wikipedia); sovereign Prussia unchanged. Civil registration 1 Oct 1874 not checked here.

1920.why: Treaty of Versailles took effect 10 Jan 1920; the Free City of Danzig was founded 15 Nov 1920 under the League of Nations, Poland running its foreign affairs, customs and railways, 'distinct from both' Germany and Poland (Wikipedia). The era table jumps from 1919 to 1920, so 1919 in the 1871 era end is a gap year. Province of Pomerania had a small territorial adjustment (about 9.5 km2 to Poland, 74 km2 of West Prussia added).

1939.why: Danzig: the Free City was annexed by Germany on 1 Sept 1939 (infobox) or formally in Oct 1939 (text) per Wikipedia, so sources differ; the Oct 1939 decrees annexed western Poland (Occupation of Poland page). BUT Pomerania proper (Stettin, Koslin) was German throughout 1920-1945, so 'German occupation' only applies to Danzig and the Polish corridor. Whether the annexation was recognised is not stated in fetched pages.

1945.why: Province of Pomerania disestablished 1945; the Oder-Neisse line split it, the western part went to East German Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, the larger eastern part to Poland (Szczecin Voivodeship); Potsdam placed it under Polish administration provisionally (2 Aug 1945); the border was recognised by the GDR 1950, West Germany 1970/72 (with reservations) and in the 1990 treaty (ratified 1992). Danzig taken by Polish and Soviet troops in March 1945.

1000.why: Stephen I was crowned on either 25 Dec 1000 or 1 Jan 1001 (Wikipedia); infobox says established 1000. Conditions on the ground in 1000 not assessed from fetched pages.

1526.why: Battle of Mohacs 1526: both the Habsburgs and the Zapolya family claimed the whole kingdom; Zapolya ruled the Eastern Hungarian Kingdom, the Habsburgs the west. Ottomans took Buda only in 1541 and the three-way division followed (Wikipedia).

1699.why: Treaty of Karlowitz 26 Jan 1699; Buda had been retaken in 1686; the Banat of Temesvar stayed Ottoman until the Treaty of Passarowitz 1718, and Transylvania was nominally independent under Austrian governors (Wikipedia). No competing claimant for the post-1699 core.

1867.why: Compromise ratified by the restored Hungarian Diet 29 May 1867, Franz Joseph crowned King of Hungary 8 June 1867 (Wikipedia). It restored the pre-1848 constitution only partly; the 1848 April Laws were a prior step.

1918.why: Hungary lost control of about 75% of its territory between late 1918 and early 1919 under armistice demarcation lines (13 Nov 1918 Belgrade); Hungarian Soviet Republic 21 March 1919; Romania ignored the June 1919 ceasefire; Trianon signed 4 June 1920 under protest, ratified 16 Nov 1920, in force 26 July 1921 (Wikipedia). Three candidate dates 1918/1920/1921.

1945.why: German occupation March 1944; Szalasi's Arrow Cross government (Oct 1944) and Miklos's provisional government (28 Dec 1944) each claimed to be legitimate while the Soviets set up a separate Provisional National Government in Debrecen (22 Dec 1944); armistice 20 Jan 1945, Budapest fell 13 Feb, German troops expelled 4 April 1945. The People's Republic dates from 1949 (Wikipedia), a republic from 1946.

1989.why: Wikipedia dates the People's Republic 1949-1989 and the Third Republic 1989-2012, but free elections were 1990 and Soviet troops left 1991, so the transition was gradual. Sovereignty did not change.

1200.why: 1200 is a placeholder lower bound: Wikipedia Pazin has Pazin County passing to the Counts of Gorizia in 1186 (and the Istria article puts inland Istria under the Patriarchs of Aquileia without a year). No source found on rival claimants, so contested left unassessed.

1374.why: Two independent sources give 1374 for the Habsburg takeover of the Pazin County: Wikipedia Pazin (Albert III of Gorizia bequeathed the Mitterburg estates; attached to Carniola) and Hrvatska enciklopedija (Istra: Pazin county to the Habsburgs 1374 by inheritance treaty). Wikipedia notes a brief Venetian conquest 1508-09 (War of Cambrai); not a change of sovereign.

1805.why: Dates contradicted for THIS ground. Pazin was Austrian (not Venetian) Istria. Hrvatska enciklopedija: after Pressburg 1805 only former VENETIAN Istria went to the Kingdom of Italy; the rest of Istria went to Napoleon by Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809) and the whole peninsula joined the Illyrian Provinces in 1809. Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces lists the March of Istria among the 1809 cessions. Austrian return: army entered Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska); Wikipedia Istria says 1814; so end year is also approximate. Wikipedia Pazin does not cover the Napoleonic period.

1815.why: Start is approximate: Austria re-entered Istria Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija), Wikipedia Istria dates the Austrian section 1814-1918; Congress of Vienna 1815. Polity label is anachronistic: Wikipedia Istria has Istria in the Kingdom of Illyria 1816-1849 (Friuli-Venezia Giulia article: Illyria abolished 1849, Austrian Littoral/Küstenland after); 'Austria-Hungary' only from 1867.

1918.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 after Villa Giusti armistice (3 Nov 1918; Wikipedia Treaty of Rapallo) but the formal transfer is Rapallo, 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska says 'formally confirmed 1920'). The State of SCS laid a competing claim to the eastern Adriatic 1918-20, but Italy held Istria on the ground.

1943.why: OZAK was created 10 Sept 1943 (Wikipedia Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral; 'semi-annexed', not incorporated into the Reich, Pula and Fiume provinces included). The Pazin district NOO decided on 13 Sept 1943 for union with Croatia (Hrvatska enciklopedija), so partisans held the ground before German reconquest; Italian (RSI) sovereignty was nominal. End 1945: partisans entered Pazin May 1945 (Wikipedia Pazin).

1945.why: Yugoslav partisans took most of Istria in 1945 and entered Pazin in May 1945 (Wikipedia Istria, Pazin); the Morgan Line (June 1945) put most of Istria in Yugoslav-administered Zone B (Wikipedia Morgan Line); Italy's cession is the Paris treaty, signed 10 Feb 1947, in force 15 Sept 1947. So 1945 de facto vs 1947 de jure. No Allied enclave in central Istria.

1991.why: Croatia declared independence 25 June 1991, moratorium, ties severed 8 Oct 1991, EEC recognition 15 Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); the JNA withdrew from Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska enciklopedija). No fighting in Istria is described.

1200.why: 1200 is a placeholder lower bound. Wikipedia Pula: Patriarchate of Aquileia gained Pula under the Peace of Treviso 1291; Rovinj was Aquileian from 1209 (Wikipedia Rovinj) but Venetian from 1283 (Wikipedia Rovinj, Hrvatska enciklopedija); Pula rose against Venice in 1145 (Wikipedia Istria). Venice and Aquileia held neighbouring towns at once.

1331.why: Pula to Venice 1331 (Wikipedia Pula; Hrvatska enciklopedija), held until 1797. But Rovinj was Venetian from 1283 (Wikipedia Rovinj; Hrvatska: 'Rovinj i Piran 1283', also 1331), so 1331 is a Pula date, not region-wide.

1797.why: Campo Formio 17 Oct 1797 gives Istria to Austria (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Pula 1797). End is approximate: Pressburg signed 26 Dec 1805 (Wikipedia) but Istria incorporated into Kingdom of Italy 1806 (Wikipedia Istria: 1806-1810).

1805.why: Contradicted label. Kingdom of Italy included Istria from the Pressburg treaty (26 Dec 1805; annexation announced 30 Mar 1806, ratified 1 May 1806) until it was ceded to France under Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809), effective 10 June 1810 (Wikipedia Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy); Hrvatska enciklopedija: 1805-1809 Kingdom of Italy, 1809 Illyrian Provinces. Austria returned Oct 1813 / 1814 (Hrvatska).

1813.why: Start approximate: Austrian army entered Istria Oct 1813, Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); Wikipedia Pula says 1813, Istria/Poreč pages 1814, Umag page 1815. Label 'Küstenland' is anachronistic before 1849 (Kingdom of Illyria 1816-49, Wikipedia Istria).

1918.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 (Villa Giusti armistice 3 Nov 1918) but formal cession is Rapallo, 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia Treaty of Rapallo; Hrvatska). Rovinj page gives 1918 for Italy, Pula page 1918. Competing SCS claim 1918-20 was diplomatic; Italy held the ground.

1943.why: German occupation of Pula after Italy's 1943 collapse (Wikipedia Pula); OZAK created 10 Sept 1943 incl. Pola province (Wikipedia OZAK); partisans proclaimed union with Croatia Sept 1943 (Hrvatska). Italian sovereignty nominal; ends spring 1945.

1945.why: Pula was an Allied (AMG) enclave inside Yugoslav Zone B from June 1945 (Wikipedia Morgan Line; Wikipedia Pula: AMG two years); Pula came under Yugoslav administration 15/16 Sept 1947 (Wikipedia Pula says 15 Sept; Hrvatska enciklopedija says 16 Sept). Rest of southern Istria Yugoslav from 1945. Wikipedia Pula itself contradicts itself ('administered by Yugoslavia since 1945').

1991.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, independence effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); JNA left Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska). No fighting in Istria described.

1200.why: 1200 is a placeholder lower bound. Wikipedia Istria: Aquileian patriarchs held inland Istria; coastal communes joined Venice from 1267. No source found on rival claimants in the west before 1267.

1331.why: Contradicted for THIS ground. Wikipedia Istria: Poreč formally to Venice 15 Feb 1267, Umag 1269, Novigrad 1270, Rovinj 1283; Hrvatska enciklopedija: Poreč 1267, Rovinj 1283, Pula 1331; Wikipedia Poreč 1267 'first Istrian city'; Umag 1269 (Wikipedia Umag); Buje 1358-1797 (Wikipedia Buje). 1331 is Pula's date. Gradual, 1267-1358. No source on rivalry.

1797.why: Campo Formio 17 Oct 1797 gives Istria to Austria (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Buje). End approximate: Pressburg 26 Dec 1805 vs Kingdom of Italy from 1806 (Wikipedia Istria 1806-1810). Wikipedia Umag wrongly says French 1797-1815.

1805.why: Contradicted label. Kingdom of Italy included Istria from the Pressburg treaty (26 Dec 1805; annexation announced 30 Mar 1806, ratified 1 May 1806) until it was ceded to France under Schönbrunn (14 Oct 1809), effective 10 June 1810 (Wikipedia Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy); Hrvatska enciklopedija: 1805-1809 Kingdom of Italy, 1809 Illyrian Provinces. Austria returned Oct 1813 / 1814 (Hrvatska). Wikipedia Poreč: Kingdom of Italy then Illyrian Provinces.

1813.why: Start approximate: Austria returned Oct 1813 / Treaty of Paris 1814 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); Wikipedia Poreč '1814', Buje and Umag '1815'. 'Küstenland' anachronistic before 1849 (Kingdom of Illyria 1816-49).

1918.why: Italy held Istria by end 1918 (Villa Giusti armistice 3 Nov 1918); formal cession Rapallo 12 Nov 1920 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska). Wikipedia Poreč, Buje, Rovinj, Umag all give 1918 for Italian rule.

1943.why: OZAK created 10 Sept 1943 (Wikipedia OZAK); Pazin decisions 13 Sept 1943 and partisan rising before German reconquest (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Istria). Italian sovereignty nominal.

1945.why: Buje district (Buje, Umag, Novigrad) was in Zone B of the Free Territory of Trieste under Yugoslav army administration from 1947 until 1954 (Wikipedia Buje, Umag; Wikipedia Free Territory of Trieste: Italy and Yugoslavia both claimed the territory until the 1954 London Memorandum, Osimo 1975). Elsewhere Yugoslav from 1945, ceded 1947 (Wikipedia Rovinj, Poreč).

1991.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia); JNA left Istria 6 Dec 1991 (Hrvatska). The Croatia-Slovenia dispute (Dragonja valley, Piran Bay, 2017 arbitration, Croatia rejects) is on the northern edge; Wikipedia does not name Poreč, Umag, Buje as disputed.

1200.why: 1200 is a placeholder. Hrvatska enciklopedija (Vinodol): Andrew II granted Vinodol to Count Guido of Krk (Frankopan) 1260; Senj Frankopan from 1271 (Senj). Rijeka was not Frankopan: Habsburgs took it from the Walsee counts 1466 (Hrvatska Rijeka; Wikipedia Rijeka). No source on disputes.

1469.why: Contradicted. 1469 is Matthias Corvinus's army taking Senj and founding the Senj captaincy (Hrvatska enciklopedija: Senj) - Hungarian-Croatian crown, not Habsburg. Rijeka went to the Habsburgs in 1466 (Wikipedia Rijeka; Hrvatska). Vinodol stayed Frankopan, divided with Zrinski 1577, to the Habsburg crown only in 1671 (Hrvatska Vinodol). Senj returned to the Military Frontier 1776 (Hrvatska Senj). The three grounds differ; contested not assessed (Uskok war with Venice ended 1617, Wikipedia Senj, but no source on who held title).

1809.why: Illyrian Provinces created by Schönbrunn 14 Oct 1809 (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces; Hrvatska Vinodol: 1809-1813). End approximate: Fiume held by the British navy 3 July-26 Aug 1813 then Austrian (Wikipedia list of governors of Fiume); Austria's recovery 1813-14, Treaty of Paris 30 May 1814, Vienna 1815 (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces); Wikipedia Rijeka infobox gives 1809-1816.

1813.why: Contradicted/split. Fiume was in the Kingdom of Illyria 1813/1816-1822, returned to Hungary 1822 (Wikipedia Corpus separatum); Hrvatska enciklopedija says 1822 'returned to Croatia'; incorporated into Croatia 31 Aug 1848 (Jelačić) until 1868; the Croatian-Hungarian Settlement of 17 Nov 1868 left Fiume's status open (Croatian text) vs corpus separatum (Hungarian text). Vinodol: Illyria to 1822, then Rijeka governorate; Croatian from 1848 (Hrvatska Vinodol). Senj: Military Frontier until 1881 (Wikipedia Senj; Croatian Military Frontier). 'Austria-Hungary' only from 1867; 'governed from Budapest from 1779' omits 1809-22 and 1848-68.

1918.why: Fiume: Hungarian suzerainty ended 29 Oct 1918; Italy and SCS disputed it; D'Annunzio 12 Sept 1919-Dec 1920; Rapallo 12 Nov 1920 made a Free State (Zanella, Fascist coup 3 Mar 1922); Treaty of Rome 27 Jan 1924, effective 22 Feb 1924 (Wikipedia Free State of Fiume; Wikipedia Rijeka says 16 Mar 1924). Sušak went to Yugoslavia 1924 (Wikipedia Sušak, Rijeka). So Italy held Fiume de jure only from 1924. Sources not fetched on Senj/Vinodol/Bakar/Crikvenica 1918-41 (believed Yugoslav, unverified).

1943.why: Fiume province in OZAK from Sept 1943 (Wikipedia OZAK; Rijeka). Partisans took Senj in fall 1943 and the Luftwaffe bombed it (Wikipedia Senj); Italian sovereignty nominal. End: Yugoslav troops entered Rijeka 3 May 1945 (Hrvatska enciklopedija Rijeka).

1945.why: Partisans entered Rijeka 3 May 1945; Morgan Line placed Rijeka in Yugoslav Zone B (Wikipedia Morgan Line); Paris Peace Treaty 1947 formally ceded it (Hrvatska Rijeka; Wikipedia Rijeka). Rijeka and Sušak merged 1948 (Wikipedia Sušak: council election 1 Feb 1948; Hrvatska says 1947). 1945 de facto vs 1947 de jure.

1991.why: Declaration 25 June 1991, effective 8 Oct 1991, recognition Jan 1992 (Wikipedia Independence of Croatia). No source found on the Kvarner situation in 1991, so contested unassessed.

1200.why: 1200 is a placeholder; Patriarchate of Aquileia recognised as an Imperial State 1077 (Wikipedia Carnia, it.wikipedia Carnia). No source found on rival claimants.

1420.why: Udine surrendered to Venice 4 June (it.wikipedia Carnia) or 7 June 1420 (Wikipedia Patria del Friuli); patriarch lost temporal power 7 July 1420; Tolmezzo followed soon after; Carnia 'by 1420' (Wikipedia Carnia). One year across sources. End: fall of Venice 12 May 1797 (magicoveneto).

1797.why: Venice fell 12 May 1797, Campo Formio 17 Oct 1797, Austrian administration installed 11 Jan 1798 (magicoveneto.it). End: Pressburg 26 Dec 1805 (Wikipedia); Carnia annexed to Kingdom of Italy 1805 (it.wikivoyage Tolmezzo) or 1806 (annexation announced 30 Mar 1806, Wikipedia Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy). Gap in the data: Carnia has no era for 1805.

1806.why: Start 1805 (Pressburg; Friuli-Venezia Giulia article, Wikivoyage) vs 1806 (annexation 30 Mar/1 May 1806, Wikipedia). End: Austrian return late 1813/1814 (Museo civico Vicenza; walter-us Udine: 1813 or 1814), Austria occupied Milan 28 Apr 1814, Lombardy-Venetia announced 12 June 1814, Vienna 1815. Sources differ by year at both ends.

1815.why: Start approximate: Austrian occupation 1813-14 and Lombardy-Venetia announced 1814, formal 1815 (Wikipedia Friuli-Venezia Giulia; magicoveneto '1814/1848 second Austrian rule'). End: Treaty of Vienna 3 Oct 1866, transfer to Italy 19 Oct, plebiscite 21-22 Oct 1866 (Wikipedia Treaty of Vienna 1866); it.wikipedia Carnia: annexed 21 Oct 1866.

1866.why: Start: single year 1866 (3 Oct treaty, 19 Oct transfer, plebiscite 21-22 Oct 1866; it.wikipedia Carnia 21 Oct 1866). BUT the era hides 1943-45 on this ground: Udine province was in OZAK from 10 Sept 1943 (Wikipedia OZAK); Kosakenland in Carnia July 1944-May 1945 under OZAK, capital Tolmezzo (Wikipedia Cossack/Kosakenland); the partisan Free Zone of Carnia, ~40 mountain comuni, July-Dec 1944, seat Ampezzo (it.wikipedia Carnia; Uniud/ANPI).

1500.why: 1500 is a lower bound (register survival), not a change of sovereignty: Carniola passed to the Habsburgs in 1335 and became a duchy in 1364 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia agrees on 1335), and was a Habsburg land continuously after. Wikipedia gives 1564 for Inner Austria as a separate unit, so 'Inner Austria' is not right for 1500-1564. End 1784 is the Josephine register reform (patent of 20 Feb 1784 per search snippets of a Czech legal encyclopedia and the Styrian Matrikenkatalog; page not fetched). Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/kranjska

1784.why: 1784 is an administrative register reform (patent 20 Feb 1784, making registration a state matter; a FEEFHS newsletter says the tabular form was adopted 1770 and modified 1784), not a change of sovereignty, so the year is approximate as a regime boundary. Carniola stayed Habsburg throughout. The 1809 end is the Treaty of Schonbrunn (14 Oct 1809), clean. Sources only seen as search snippets (feefhs.org 2017Apr newsletter; katholische-kirche-steiermark.at Matrikenkatalog); the Czech page fetched empty.

1809.why: Start: Treaty of Schonbrunn 14 Oct 1809 created the Illyrian Provinces (Wikipedia); Hrvatska enciklopedija also says Kranjska was an Illyrian province from 1809. End is not clean: Austria retook territory from Aug-Nov 1813 (Trieste 29 Oct 1813), the Treaty of Paris was 1814, and the formal Austrian annexation is dated 9 June 1815 (Wikipedia gives 1809-1814/1815; Duchy of Carniola infobox says restored 1815). De facto 1813 vs de jure 1815 is a gap over a year. Sovereignty itself not disputed. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/kranjska

1813.why: Start: Austrian reconquest in autumn 1813 de facto, 1814 Paris, 9 June 1815 formal (Wikipedia, Illyrian Provinces); Kingdom of Illyria only from 1816 (Hrvatska enciklopedija). End: Duchy of Carniola ceased 29 Oct 1918 (Wikipedia infobox) but the borders were settled by Saint-Germain (10 Sept 1919) and Rapallo (12 Nov 1920). Habsburg rule itself undisputed in between. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/kranjska

1918.why: Contested ground: Slovenian National Assembly claimed southern Carinthia on 17 Oct 1918, Yugoslav forces entered Carinthia from 5 Nov 1918, fighting followed, Entente forced Maister's men out 28 May 1919, Saint-Germain was 10 Sept 1919 and the plebiscite 10 Oct 1920 (59.1% for Austria). The Julian March (inside the ring: Gorizia, Trieste, Postojna) went to Italy at Rapallo, 12 Nov 1920. So the 1918 start and the real borders differ by 1-2 years. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rapallo_(1920)

1941.why: Split among occupiers from April 1941: Germany (Upper Carniola, Lower Styria), Italy (Province of Ljubljana, formal annexation dated 3 May 1941 on Wikipedia), Hungary (Prekmurje), with smaller slices to the Independent State of Croatia (Wikipedia Slovenia in WWII). German formal annexation was postponed. After the Italian armistice (Sept 1943) Germany took the Province of Ljubljana and the Littoral; the Partisans held liberated territory (Kocevje) and Ljubljana's liberation was announced 9 May 1945, last battle 14-15 May. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Province_of_Ljubljana

1945.why: Yugoslav state from May 1945, but the Julian March part of the ring was disputed: Allied/Yugoslav zones from June 1945, Free Territory of Trieste 1947, Zone A to Italy and Zone B to Yugoslavia in 1954 (London Memorandum, 5 Oct 1954), border settled by the Treaty of Osimo in 1975 (Wikipedia: Free Territory of Trieste was 'an object of dispute between Italy and Yugoslavia'). End 1991: independence declared 25 June 1991, Brioni Accord 7 July postponed it three months, JNA withdrawal completed 25-26 Oct 1991, EC recognition 15 Jan 1992. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ten-Day_War

1991.why: Declared independence 25 June 1991; Ten-Day War 27 June-7 July; Brioni Accord postponed independence for three months; JNA withdrew by 25-26 Oct 1991; EC recognition 15 Jan 1992; UN membership 22 May 1992 (Wikipedia, Ten-Day War). Federal sovereignty was practically contested in 1991, so both approx and contested are true for the start year. From 1992 uncontested.

1200.why: 1200 is a floor (before registers), not an event. Hrvatska enciklopedija: Coloman crowned king of Croatia and Dalmatia at Biograd 1102; Venetian claims ended by the Peace of Zadar 1358; Venice bought Ladislaus of Naples's claims in 1409. So rival claimants (Venice, Hungary-Croatia, Naples, Bosnia) fought over the towns through the whole era. Independent source for the 1420 end: Wikipedia 'Venetian Dalmatia' (control 'fully consolidated in 1420').

1420.why: Start: Venetian sale of claims 1409 (Hrvatska enciklopedija, Wikipedia), 'fully consolidated' 1420, so 1420 is the end of conquest, not a single change. End 1797 clean: Treaty of Campo Formio (17-18 Oct 1797). Contested because the hinterland inside the ring stayed Ottoman for most of the era: Imotski was Ottoman from 1492/1493 to 1717 (Wikipedia, Hrvatska enciklopedija), so Venice did not hold the whole ring; Venice held only the coast and islands. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venetian_Dalmatia

1797.why: Start: Venice fell and Austria obtained Dalmatia at Campo Formio (17-18 Oct 1797; Hrvatska enciklopedija and Wikipedia Kingdom of Dalmatia). End: Peace of Pressburg 26 Dec 1805 transferred Dalmatia, France took control in February 1806 (Hrvatska enciklopedija), so end 1805 vs 1806 differ. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1805.why: Start 1805 (Pressburg) vs actual French takeover Feb 1806. End: Austria retook Dalmatia from 1813 (Zadar surrendered 6 Dec 1813, Kotor 3 Jan 1814, Ragusa Jan 1814), the Illyrian Provinces are dated 1809-1814/1815 on Wikipedia, with formal annexation 9 June 1815. Contested: the British held the Dalmatian islands until July 1815 and Russian/Montenegrin forces held Boka in 1806-07; French and Austrians both held towns in 1813. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1814.why: Start is a process: Austrian takeover 1813 (Tomasic), Illyrian dissolution 1814, Congress of Vienna confirmation and Kingdom of Dalmatia 1815 (Wikipedia: infobox 1815-1918; Hrvatska enciklopedija: 1815). End 1918: Kingdom ended 29 Oct 1918 when the Croatian Sabor joined the State of SCS, but Italian forces reached Vis, Lastovo and Sibenik on 5-6 Nov 1918 and occupied a Zadar-Sibenik strip and islands by end 1918. Austrian rule itself undisputed in between. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1918.why: Italian army occupied Zadar on 4 Nov 1918 and a coastal strip Zadar-Sibenik plus islands (Hvar, Vis, Korcula, Mljet, Lastovo, Pag) by end 1918; the Treaty of Rapallo (12 Nov 1920) gave Italy Zadar, Lastovo, Palagruza, Cres and Losinj. The rest of Dalmatia was Yugoslav. The Kingdom of Dalmatia ended 29 Oct 1918; Yugoslav kingdom proclaimed 1 Dec 1918. End 1941: Axis invasion April 1941. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Rapallo_(1920)

1941.why: Italy occupied in April 1941 (Wikipedia Governorate of Dalmatia: created April 1941, infobox 18 May 1941; Hrvatska enciklopedija: Treaties of Rome 18 May 1941; first governor 16 April / Bastianini 7 June). Italy dissolved the governorate administratively 19 Aug 1943; infobox disestablishment 10 Sept 1943 after the 8 Sept armistice. Contested: Mussolini's occupation overrode the NDH, which kept nominal control of parts and disputed it. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1943.why: After 8 Sept 1943 Partisans briefly took much of Dalmatia then withdrew before German forces (Hrvatska enciklopedija); the NDH on 10 Sept 1943 declared the Treaties of Rome void and annexed the ceded Dalmatian territory, though Germany blocked its claim on Zadar, which stayed nominally Italian under German protection until 1944; Partisans liberated all of Dalmatia by end 1944 and the last Italian authority (Zadar prefect) left 30 Oct 1944 (Wikipedia: Governorate of Dalmatia). Zadar was taken 1 Nov 1944. Several authorities held the ground in these 18 months. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zadar

1945.why: Start: Partisans liberated Dalmatia progressively by end 1944 (Split-based Croatian government formed 14 April 1945; Hrvatska enciklopedija); Zadar captured 1 Nov 1944 but only officially became Yugoslav/Croatian in 1947 (Wikipedia: Zadar). End: Croatian independence declared 25 June 1991, effective only after the Brioni three-month postponement (7 Jul 1991 -> Oct 1991) and Dalmatian hinterland partly held by Serb forces from 1991. So both ends fuzzy. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1991.why: Independence 25 June 1991, postponed three months at Brioni (7 July 1991), effective October 1991; the Serb-proclaimed SAO Krajina (northern Dalmatia, Lika, from 21 Dec 1990) and then the Republic of Serbian Krajina covered 13,913 sq km (more than a quarter of Croatia) in 1992-95, including Knin inside the Dalmatia ring, until Operation Storm in 1995. The RSK was not recognised by any state. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_War_of_Independence

1553.why: Origins are gradual: Hrvatska enciklopedija says the Krajina formed 'during the 1520s', Vienna War Council 1556, split into Croatian and Slavonian commands 1568, Bruck Sabor 1578; Wikipedia infobox gives 1553. No single year. Contested because much of the ring was Ottoman for most of the era: Lika was Ottoman from 1527 (Udbina) until 1689 and the Ottomans held Donji Lapac until 1791 (Wikipedia: Lika); Karlowitz (1699) set the border; the Frontier also ranked above the ban and Sabor (jurisdictional contest, 1556 and 1630). Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Frontier ; further: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lika

1746.why: No source gives 1746: Wikipedia says the Slavonian Frontier was established 1745 and the Banat Frontier 1751, with the Vlach Statute abolished 1737; Hrvatska enciklopedija says 'mid-18th century' the captaincies were replaced by 11 regiments and the Military Krajina Rights were issued in 1754. So 1746 is approximate. Habsburg control of the Frontier itself was not disputed in this period, though the Ottomans held Donji Lapac to 1791. Napoleonic note: the Illyrian Provinces 1809-1813 included Croatian lands southwest of the Sava (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces), which covers Military Croatia. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojna-krajina

1848.why: 1848 is a political turning point (serfdom abolished, Jelacic becomes commander, krajisnik representatives demand union with civil Croatia: Hrvatska enciklopedija), not a change of sovereignty. Demilitarisation was gradual: Basic Laws 1850, Transylvanian Frontier 1851/53, Krizevci and Djurdjevac regiments 1 Aug 1871, cordon abolished 1872, Banat Frontier 8 Aug 1873, rest 1881. Command stayed in Vienna, so who held the ground was not in dispute, though Croatian and Hungarian estates claimed it. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_Frontier

1881.why: Imperial manifesto of incorporation 15 July 1881 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Military Frontier and Croatia-Slavonia agree), effective 1 Aug 1881; Lika restored to Croatia-Slavonia on 15 July 1881 (Wikipedia: Lika). End 1918: the Croatian Sabor proclaimed independence and joined the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs on 29 Oct 1918 (Wikipedia), union into the Kingdom of SCS 1 Dec 1918. Both within weeks, one year. Banat Frontier (outside the ring) was abolished earlier, 1873. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojna-krajina

1918.why: Sabor decision 29 Oct 1918 and union 1 Dec 1918 (Wikipedia: Croatia-Slavonia, Banat/Backa/Baranja page) are in one year; Kingdom of Yugoslavia renamed 3 Oct 1929. End 1941: Axis invasion 6 April 1941, NDH proclaimed 10 April 1941 (Wikipedia). Both clean for the Krajina ground, with the proviso that Srijem was entered by Serbian forces in Nov 1918. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_State_of_Croatia

1941.why: NDH proclaimed 10 April 1941; Italy held a south-west zone and Germany a north-east zone until Sept 1943, then Germany the whole NDH; Partisans controlled large areas (Lika, Kordun, Banija included), Chetniks made agreements with the NDH. Control was split. End 1945: NDH dissolved 8 May, forces surrendered at Bleiburg 15 May, Battle of Odzak 25 May 1945; the Syrmian Front held Srijem until 12 April 1945. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrmian_Front

1945.why: Start fuzzy: Srijem liberated only on 12 April 1945 (Syrmian Front), the NDH ended 8-25 May 1945. End 1991: Croatia declared independence 25 June 1991, postponed three months (Brioni 7 July 1991), effective Oct 1991. Within the era the ground was uncontested Yugoslav (SR Croatia/SR Serbia). Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrmian_Front

1991.why: SAO Krajina proclaimed 21 Dec 1990 (northern Dalmatia, Lika), RSK declared 1991 and held 13,913 sq km in 1992-95 including Banija/Kordun/Lika/West Slavonia, unrecognised by any state, UN Protected Areas in Croatian territory; Operations Flash and Storm in 1995 recovered most; Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) returned by Jan 1998. Independence itself was declared 25 June 1991, postponed to Oct 1991 (Brioni). Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Serbian_Krajina

1493.why: Start: Wikipedia says held by the Ottomans 'from the fall of Bosnia in 1492'; Hrvatska enciklopedija says 1493 ('od 1493'); a tourism site says only '15th century'. End: Imotski liberated by Venice 2 Aug 1717 (Mocenigo; Wikipedia, Total Croatia News), clean. I could not verify 'Sanjak of Klis': the Wikipedia Sanjak of Klis page (founded 12 March 1537) does not mention Imotski; the Ottoman administrative assignment is unverified. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/imotski

1717.why: Venice took Imotski on 2 Aug 1717 (Wikipedia, Hrvatska enciklopedija 'od 1717'); the Treaty of Passarowitz (21 July 1718) then confirmed it, with Venice gaining 'Imotski and Vrgorac' (Wikipedia: Passarowitz). So 1717 conquest vs 1718 treaty. End 1797: Campo Formio (17-18 Oct 1797), clean. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/imotski

1797.why: Start 1797 Campo Formio is clean (Hrvatska enciklopedija). End: Pressburg 26 Dec 1805 but French took control in Feb 1806 (Hrvatska enciklopedija dalmacija), so 1805 vs 1806. Hrvatska enciklopedija on Imotski gives 'Habsburg rule 1797-1918, interrupted by a short French administration 1805-13'. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/dalmacija

1805.why: French administration 1805-1813 per Hrvatska enciklopedija (Imotski); actual French takeover Feb 1806, and the Austrian reconquest of Dalmatia ran 1813-1814 (Zadar 6 Dec 1813, Kotor Jan 1814), with formal annexation 9 June 1815 (Wikipedia Illyrian Provinces). Imotski is inland so the British island occupation did not touch it. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/imotski

1814.why: Start fuzzy: reconquest 1813, 1814, Kingdom of Dalmatia and Congress of Vienna 1815. End 1918 clean for Imotski: Kingdom of Dalmatia ended 29 Oct 1918, the Italian occupation of 1918 was a coastal strip Zadar-Sibenik plus islands (Wikipedia: Rapallo, Kingdom of Dalmatia), not inland Imotski. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Dalmatia

1918.why: Start clean (29 Oct 1918, 1 Dec 1918). Contested within the era: 1941-45 Imotski was in the Independent State of Croatia (Wikipedia: Imotski), with Partisans controlling large areas (NDH page); the era merges 1941-45 into Yugoslavia. End 1991: independence 25 June 1991, postponed three months at Brioni, effective Oct 1991. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imotski

1991.why: Start approximate: Croatia declared independence 25 June 1991, postponed three months at Brioni on 7 July 1991 (Wikipedia, Ten-Day War), so effective October 1991. Contested left unassessed: I found no source stating whether any part of Imotska krajina was outside Croatian control in 1991-95 (a Croatian army brigade of Imotski fought near Dubrovnik per predsjednik.hr; that does not settle it). Absence is not evidence.

1463.why: Kingdom of Bosnia fell 1463 (Hrvatska enciklopedija, Wikipedia), but conquest was piecemeal: Hungary held Jajce (Banate of Jajce) until 1527, Usora and forts south of the Sava into the 1530s, the Duchy of Herzegovina fell 1481-1482/83 (Wikipedia: Bosnia Eyalet says 1483; Hrvatska enciklopedija 1482), Bihac fell 1592. Eyalet only from 1580 (Ferhad Pasha Sokolovic), Bosnia Vilayet by 1867; before 1580 it was a sanjak. Also under Habsburg strips of Posavina 1718-1739 (Passarowitz). End 1878 clean: Congress of Berlin 13 July 1878, occupation 29 July-20 Oct 1878. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ottoman_conquest_of_Bosnia_and_Herzegovina ; further: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_Eyalet

1878.why: Start: Congress of Berlin placed Bosnia and Herzegovina under Austro-Hungarian administration while formally under Ottoman sovereignty; military occupation 29 July-20 Oct 1878 (Wikipedia, Austro-Hungarian rule). End: annexation announced 5 Oct 1908 (7 Oct in Sarajevo), Ottoman recognition Feb 1909. Contested because sovereignty and administration were split for 30 years (Ottoman sovereignty vs Austro-Hungarian rule); a joint Serb-Muslim uprising in 1882 was put down. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1908.why: Annexation 5-7 Oct 1908 (Wikipedia; Hrvatska enciklopedija 1908), recognised by the Ottomans in Feb 1909 and by the powers afterwards (Bosnian crisis, but no change of holder on the ground). End 1918: governor's term ended 3 Nov 1918 and the Kingdom of SCS was formed 1 Dec 1918 (Wikipedia gives 1 Dec 1918 as the end of rule); Hrvatska enciklopedija says 1918. Same year. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1918.why: Bosnia entered the new Yugoslav state in 1918 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia Austro-Hungarian rule gives 1 Dec 1918 for the end of rule). End: Yugoslavia invaded 6 April 1941 and Bosnia was included in the NDH after the capitulation on 17 April 1941 (Hrvatska enciklopedija). Both in the same year. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1941.why: Bosnia included in the NDH after 17 April 1941 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); Germans and Italians held zones until Sept 1943 and Partisans, Chetniks and the NDH fought over the ground, so control was contested (Wikipedia, NDH: 'control was divided'). End 1945: ZAVNOBiH third session in Sarajevo April 1945; NDH dissolved 8 May and finished 25 May 1945. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1945.why: Bosnia became a republic in postwar Yugoslavia, with the third ZAVNOBiH session in Sarajevo in April 1945 (Hrvatska enciklopedija); end: independence referendum 29 Feb-1 Mar 1992, declaration 3 March 1992, recognition 6 April (Wikipedia) or 7 April 1992 (Hrvatska enciklopedija), all in one year. The tail of the era saw rival bodies set up (Herzeg-Bosnia 18 Nov 1991; Republic of the Serbian People 9 Jan 1992), but control of the ground did not change until the war. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1992.why: Independence declared 3 March 1992, recognised 6/7 April 1992, UN membership 22 May 1992. War 1992-95: Bosnian Serbs held about 70% in 1992, Croat forces held Herzeg-Bosnia, the Bosnian government held the rest; Croat-Bosniak fighting from 1993, Washington Agreement 1994, Dayton initialled 21 Nov and signed 14 Dec 1995 (Wikipedia, Bosnian War). Competing authorities, so contested; the 1992-95 war explains the 'reconstructed registers' warning. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/bosna-i-hercegovina

1526.why: Start approximate: Mohacs 1526, but Hrvatska enciklopedija says Srijem was subdued by 1529, Backa by 1540 and Banat by 1551-52. Contested: Jovan Nenad's brief Serb state 1526-27 (Wikipedia, History of Vojvodina). End approximate: Backa and part of Srijem passed to the Habsburgs in 1699 (Karlowitz), the Banat and rest of Srijem only in 1716-1718 (Passarowitz). Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina

1699.why: Karlowitz (26 Jan 1699): Habsburgs got Backa and part of Srijem, but the Ottomans kept the Banat of Temesvar until 1716-1718 (Wikipedia, Karlowitz and Passarowitz; Hrvatska enciklopedija says 1716-18), so the polity split the ground for 17-19 years. End 1848: Serb assembly at Karlovci 13-15 May 1848 demanded a Serbian Vojvodina; the Frontier organisation began breaking up (Hrvatska enciklopedija 1741-51 dissolved the Danube/Tisa/Sava frontiers, Banat Frontier lasted to 1848). Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Karlowitz ; further: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina

1848.why: Serb assembly May 1848 proclaimed an autonomous Serbian Vojvodina (self-proclaimed, per Wikipedia), imperial crown land created 1849 (constitution of 4 March 1849 confirmed it, Hrvatska enciklopedija), abolished 27 Dec 1860 (Hrvatska enciklopedija; Wikipedia body says 1860 but infobox 1861), direct Hungarian rule only from 1867 (Wikipedia). So 1848 was a contested start amid Hungarian revolution, and the changes of 1849, 1860, 1867 are all inside the era. Syrmia went to Croatia-Slavonia in 1867. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina

1918.why: Serbian forces entered Novi Sad 9 Nov 1918, dismantled the Banat Republic (proclaimed 31 Oct) on 15 Nov, assembly voted union with Serbia on 25 Nov 1918, Kingdom of SCS 1 Dec 1918; the exact borders were set by the peace conference: eastern Banat to Romania 1919, northern Backa/Baranya to Hungary 1920 (Wikipedia: Banat, Backa and Baranja). Sovereignty was in question until Trianon. End 1941: Axis invasion 6 April 1941. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banat,_Ba%C4%8Dka_and_Baranja

1941.why: Partition (Hrvatska enciklopedija, Wikipedia): Srijem to the NDH, Backa to Hungary, Banat under German military administration in Serbia but de facto under its ethnic German minority. End: Red Army and Partisans took the Banat and Backa in autumn 1944, but the Syrmian Front held western Srijem until 12 April 1945. Also: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axis_occupation_of_Vojvodina

1944.why: Start 1944: autumn 1944 for Banat and Backa, April 1945 for Srijem (Syrmian Front breakthrough 12 April 1945). Autonomous province: Hrvatska enciklopedija says delimited from Croatia and joined Serbia as an autonomous province in 1945-46; Wikipedia says 1945. The military administration period was not verified. Since then no competing authority was found. Also: https://www.enciklopedija.hr/clanak/vojvodina
